title: C402A — Heated rear window connector reference with a conflicting function label
introduction:
I read this connector record like a parts label with an awkward footnote: the title identifies the heated rear window element, but the Function cell says “RELAY - HEATER MIRROR.” Those names are not interchangeable. The separate Coupe heated-window wiring diagram corroborates the rear-window identity, while the conflicting Function wording stays visible in this record.

Start with the cavity label in the drawing, then read horizontally across the matching table row. That keeps the circuit, wire details and terminal reference together instead of turning the table into electrical alphabet soup.

This is a guide to reading the reference, not permission to choose a wire, probe a terminal or replace a connector. Confirm the applicable vehicle wiring and service procedure before physical work. The Gauge convention and the Box, Size, Cols and Used codes are not defined here.

edits.why: The drawing places its circular cavity label toward the right, beside a stepped section on the left. I use those landmarks to orient myself on the page and find the matching Cavity row. The illustration does not establish which physical side you should view or how to release the connector.

edits.text: Read the pin assignment and its label conflict
edits.why: Keep the circuit, wire color, Gauge and terminal part number attached to their own row. The literal mirror-relay Function label conflicts with the heated-rear-window identity above. The separate [Coupe heated-window wiring diagram](#/reference/wiring-056-001) identifies this connector at the heated rear window element and shows the mirror branches separately. That corroborates the title, but does not erase the inconsistent Function cell or turn this reference into a physical wire-selection or test procedure.

Both listed kits share the engineering shell and tin material, but their Gauge and service-part entries differ. Matching the shell is therefore not enough to choose a kit. Read each complete row as a separate catalogue record, and keep the terminal part number in the pin table distinct from the pigtail service-part number. This source gives no rule for choosing between the kits.
